dedupe_keys.name: prioritevac netlogo agent based model of evacuation from building fires based on the 2003 station nightclub fire

description: PrioritEvac simulates how people evacuated from a building fire, taking the 2003 Station Nightclub fire as its case. It was written in NetLogo by Eileen Young as part of the Interdependencies in Community Resilience (ICoR) project and passed CoMSES peer review in 2019. According to the library page, the release contains the simulation together with CSV files of data about the fire, the smoke, the building and the people involved. Version 1.0.0 is free to download from CoMSES under a CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 licence (non-commercial use) and has a DOI. Caveats: it models one historical fire, so results for other buildings need new layout and fire inputs, and the non-commercial licence limits reuse. Coverage is one building. Simulation uses: studying occupant evacuation and prioritisation in building fires, and testing egress assumptions used by fire and rescue services. Related records: the Fire Model Survey egress list (data-fire-model-survey-egress-models) places such models among engineering evacuation tools.
inputs: Building layout, fire and smoke data for the Station Nightclub
name: PrioritEvac: NetLogo agent-based model of evacuation from building fires, based on the 2003 Station Nightclub fire
outputs: Evacuation outcomes of occupants during the fire
